verdict.rationale: Glama's directory says every server is "scanned, scored," and lets developers "search, compare" servers. Community users confirm a TDQS quality score with letter grades, and the connector schema documents a verified-ownership mechanism. However, first-party documentation of how scores work and how they appear for comparison is thin, and one user reports score retests stalling for days because of an undocumented billing requirement. missing for 10: documented usage counts, documented health/liveness checks, first-party explanation of the scoring methodology and badge display, reliable score refresh.

support.subject: As a developer, I can compare servers using published quality signals — usage counts, health or liveness checks, scores, or verification badges

citations.quote: A directory of 91,626 Model Context Protocol servers and 23,749 remote connectors, every one scanned, scored,
Search, compare, and connect to thousands of MCP servers
